verification_scope: Local automated acceptance; external/deferred limits remain explicit.

I01.implementation: ORM predicates bind data; dynamic sorting and maintenance identifiers use fixed allowlists.
I01.evidence: Malicious login/register strings, literal apostrophes and invalid sorting tests; source query inventory.
I01.limitation: No independent penetration test; future raw SQL needs the same review.

I02.implementation: React renders user text as text; links are validated, PDF previews are raster images and a restrictive CSP blocks scripts.
I02.evidence: Stored names, filenames, document descriptions and quotations; explicitly mocked malicious explanation response; upload and CSP tests.
I02.limitation: XSS on a trusted origin can still read memory; these cases do not prove all future views safe.

I03.implementation: Every mutating API call requires X-BuildTrust-Request: 1; browser Origin and Fetch Metadata are checked before business handling. No auth cookies.
I03.evidence: Missing marker, foreign origin and cross-site metadata rejection tests; valid browser and API workflows.
I03.limitation: An allowed-origin script remains trusted; a stolen bearer token is not prevented by CSRF controls.

I04.implementation: Signatures, allowed types, body/file size, archive expansion, pages, child deadlines and private paths are bounded. Procurement remains untrusted until confirmed.
I04.evidence: Disguised executable/PDF/JSON fixtures, parser bounds and protected preview tests.
I04.limitation: No antivirus or complete malware-sandbox claim; human evidence can still be false.

I05.implementation: Provider requests allow exact HTTPS hosts and ports, no credentials or redirects, and ignore environment proxies. Ollama is explicitly loopback-only. Listing URLs are never fetched.
I05.evidence: Disallowed schemes, hosts, ports and credentials tests; local-model normalization and mocked provider boundaries.
I05.limitation: Paid/live providers and a real local model retain separate external acceptance.

A01.implementation: Current account and project membership are checked through shared resource helpers, including child records and protected files.
A01.evidence: Separate-project and anonymous API tests plus financial, archived-run and file browser workflows.
A01.limitation: This is application isolation, not native SQLite RLS or protection against an unrestricted DB owner.

A02.implementation: Persistent account/IP admission limits and operation budgets include MFA verification and management. Challenges allow five failed codes.
A02.evidence: Restart/limit, five-attempt, expiry and concurrent usage tests; browser clients honor Retry-After.
A02.limitation: Shared local IPs may share admission limits; this is a single-process local release.

A03.implementation: Argon2 hashes protect private passwords. Password checks run outside ordinary financial writer locks.
A03.evidence: Login, recovery and hash-preservation tests; populated-copy migration comparison.
A03.limitation: Public-demo passwords are intentionally public; offline setup needs OS protection.

A04.implementation: Private Admin/Finance MFA is mandatory; optional roles may enroll. TOTP factors are encrypted, challenges/codes hashed, replay rejected and recovery use atomic. Only the owner resets lost factors.
A04.evidence: Enrollment, restricted access, replay, expiry, concurrent code use, role changes, reset and MFA backup/restore tests; real browser enrollment/sign-in.
A04.limitation: Local automated TOTP and browser evidence is not an independent phone/interoperability or phishing-resistance assessment. Public demo is exempt.

A05.implementation: Every protected request reloads current account, role, membership and session assurance; financial execution revalidates sources and approval.
A05.evidence: Forged/weak-assurance sessions, current-role checks and original financial/permission regression tests.
A05.limitation: OS/database owner remains trusted. The copilot cannot approve or settle.

A06.implementation: SQLite uses server-side project predicates. Native database RLS has not been enabled.
A06.evidence: Architecture and project-isolation tests establish the implemented boundary only.
A06.limitation: Deferred: a future PostgreSQL migration needs native policies and acceptance.

S01.implementation: Private random JWT keys must contain at least 32 UTF-8 bytes; existing strong keys are retained. Signed tokens also need an active server session and MFA assurance when applicable.
S01.evidence: Signing/session checks, old-session revocation and preserved-key migration/restore evidence.
S01.limitation: An unrestricted host owner can read signing material; TLS is required before any remote deployment.

S02.implementation: API credentials and separate MFA encryption keys stay in protected server storage and private backups; paid dispatch is off by default.
S02.evidence: Current/history/bundle/archive scanning, private-path/exclusion tests and restored-factor access.
S02.limitation: No genuine exposed provider key was found; unavailable provider ownership would still block a required rotation.

S03.implementation: Access tokens, restricted challenges, setup keys and recovery codes remain in memory. Only harmless view filters may persist.
S03.evidence: Browser storage inspection after MFA enrollment and frontend session tests.
S03.limitation: A page refresh requires sign-in; memory storage alone cannot defeat XSS.

C01.implementation: Cross-origin access is disabled. Trusted hosts and browser origins are explicit per launcher; forwarded headers do not define trust.
C01.evidence: Foreign Origin/Host/Fetch Metadata rejection; actual isolated browser, recording and proxy configuration.
C01.limitation: A future hosted address needs deliberate configuration and HTTPS review.

C02.implementation: No incoming webhook integration or real payment callback exists; callbacks remain disabled.
C02.limitation: Not applicable now. Any future webhook needs provider-specific signatures and replay controls.

C03.implementation: Production source maps are explicitly disabled. API/static handling rejects .map requests.
C03.evidence: Built-assets check finds no map files/directives; map-request regression.
C03.limitation: Public source is intentionally available under AGPL; hiding maps is not an access-control boundary.

C04.implementation: Errors are generic with request IDs; structured logs omit tokens, passwords and content. Lockfiles and nested archives are included in redacted secret scans.
C04.evidence: Synthetic-marker log/error tests and pinned scanner output.
C04.limitation: Pattern scans cannot guarantee discovery of every possible secret format.

C05.implementation: Reproducible locks include maintained MFA libraries with attribution. Known-advisory scans cover Python and frontend dependencies.
C05.evidence: Dated npm and pip-audit runs report no known advisories.
C05.limitation: New vulnerabilities can appear; this is not a complete supply-chain or penetration assessment.
